title: GPU firmware & runtime interop notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures lab-side observations and an action-first playbook for validating GPU firmware (BIOS/Device-FW), host driver variants, CUDA runtimes, NCCL builds, and container runtime interactions across Kubernetes node images. Focus is on private/VPC deployments where vendor firmware differences and node-image stamping cause subtle regression modes we saw in Q2.

Scope and goals:
- Produce a concise compatibility table with explicit pass/fail criteria (boot, nvidia-smi, CUDA sanity, NCCL allreduce, perf +/-5%).
- Record terraform module knobs required to pin images/taints/driver metadata and a recommended canary upgrade strategy.
- Define a repeatable validation harness (lab commands, log captures, perf metrics) for each upgrade window.
- Surface open questions and rollback triggers for onprem upgrades.

Summary findings (high level):
- BIOS/FW mismatches cause ~10% of GPU initialization failures observed in lab when drivers >= 535 + CUDA12.2 are used on older firmware revisions.
- MIG-enabled boards require explicit firmware-level MIG enablement; driver-only MIG toggles (nvidia-smi) sometimes fail on older board-FW.
- Containerized driver approaches (NVIDIA-CRI + host driver) are stable for 1.26/1.27 k8s if the node-image includes nvidia-kmod/kernel headers.
- crun shows ~3% lower tail latency than runc for large-sequence tokenization jobs in our microbench; recommend validating CRI on perf-critical Dedicated clusters.

Compatibility matrix (condensed text):
Columns: node-os | k8s | bios-fw | nvidia-driver | cuda | nccl | container-runtime | result
- Ubuntu20.04 | 1.24 | FW-1.2.0 | 515.86 | 11.8 | 2.14 | runc | PASS (smoke)
- Ubuntu22.04 | 1.25 | FW-1.2.0 | 535.54 | 12.1 | 2.15 | runc | FAIL: init timeout on 2/8 nodes (FW incompat)
- Ubuntu22.04 | 1.26 | FW-1.3.1 | 555.23 | 12.2 | 2.17 | crun | PASS (full tests)
- Ubuntu22.04 | 1.27 | FW-1.1.9 | 555.23 | 12.2 | 2.17 | crun | PARTIAL (MIG assert on boot)

Pass criteria per row (applies to automation):
- Node boots, kubelet registers within 90s.
- nvidia-smi returns all GPUs and correct driver string.
- run-cuda-sanity.sh (included below) exits 0 within 3m per GPU.
- run-nccl-allreduce.sh achieves >90% of baseline across 8 GPUs (baseline from perf bench).

Validation harness and commands (lab steps):
1) node image build: stamp image label: gpu.driver=555.23, gpu.fw=FW-1.3.1, node-image:ubuntu-22-04-gpu-20251001
2) boot node in isolated test cluster (no production traffic).
3) check kernel modules: modinfo nvidia | grep -E "version:|supports"
4) smoke: docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.2.0-base-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi && /usr/local/cuda/samples/bin/x86_64/linux/release/deviceQuery
5) NCCL test: run docker image with nccl-tests and capture latency/throughput; use NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME override to test multi-nic setups.
6) MIG test: nvidia-smi -i 0 mig -cgi && verify partitions then run workload pinned to MIG device indexes.

Terraform module notes (pool/node-level):
- Variables to add/ensure: gpu_driver_version (string), gpu_fw_tag (string), node_image_tag (string), node_label_gpu_driver, node_taint_gpu_critical (bool), mig_enabled (bool), image_build_id (string).
- Lifecycle: use create_before_destroy where possible for node pools when rotating kernel/driver to avoid k8s pod disruption.
- Provider hooks: add a local-exec pre_provision step to fetch expected firmware from vendor API and attach as node annotation so operators can assert in k8s that nodes match expected firmware before joining cluster.
- Example snippet (pseudocode): set node metadata key: redwood/gpu-driver=555.23, redwood/gpu-fw=FW-1.3.1, redwood/mig=true
- Upgrade strategy: staged rollout via tf-managed pool sizes: 3 canary nodes -> wait validation -> roll remainder in batches of N where N is max(5% of pool, 3). Use taints to avoid scheduling customer traffic until validated.

Upgrade playbook (stepwise):
- Pre-checks (24-72h): collect image manifests, vendor fw release notes, kernel ABI changes. Run compatibility table lookup.
- Canary (1-2h window): deploy image to 3 nodes, run full smoke + nccl tests, compare to baseline, monitor klog and dmesg for OOMs or GPU resets.
- Ramp (6-24h): increase to 20% of pool, repeat tests, confirm telemetry stability.
- Full (rolling): batch size N as above, ensure 15m steady state between batches and automatic rollback trigger on SLO breach for 5m.

Rollback triggers (automated):
- >3 nodes fail kubelet registration in 15m
- 5%+ increase in GPU driver crashloop or GPU resets logged (dmesg + nvidia-smi reset count)
- NCCL throughput regression >10% on canary vs baseline

Observed lab anomalies (notes, unique):
- Some vendor firmware (FW-1.2.0) responds to nvidia-smi with correct PCI ids but kernel dmesg shows a deferred firmware upload that blocks driver init intermittently; this is non-deterministic and correlated with BIOS version and kernel patch level.
- In one test, container runtime seccomp profile prevented /dev/fuse access for the containerized toolkit and caused CUDA samples to fail; add test that runs with host-devices and host-cgroup capabilities.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can vendor supply a firmware diff for FW-1.2.0 -> FW-1.3.1 to confirm MIG control path fixes? (Assigned: Arjun)
- Should terraform module expose explicit firmware-assert toggle to refuse node join if firmware mismatch? (Design decision)
- Evaluate crun vs runc in production-like tokenization workload on dedicated nodes (Lina to run extended perf 48h).

Artifacts produced in lab run on 2025-09-30:
- node-image digest: sha256:abc123... (stamped as ubuntu-22-04-gpu-20250930)
- baseline nccl throughput (8xA100): 12.4 GB/s allreduce avg
- Canary failure logs attached in JIRA: INF-3241

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Add firmware annotation and terraform pre-check hook to pool module (owner: Marcus)
- Schedule vendor firmware meeting to request release notes and binary diff (owner: Arjun)
- Create automated validation job in ci-lab that runs on node image builds and posts results to Confluence page PD-interop-protocol (owner: Sofia)

Appendix: quick scripts referenced:
- run-cuda-sanity.sh: pulls cuda image, runs deviceQuery and simple memcpy bandwidth test, returns 0 on success.
- run-nccl-allreduce.sh: runs nccl-tests (allreduce) across MPI with 8 ranks, collects median latency and throughput.

Notes to reviewer: this is a working draft intended to capture the unusual role firmware plays during driver upgrades and to make terraform-side mitigations explicit. Feedback wanted on: whether firmware-assert belongs in infra-as-code or as an operator-run preflight, and whether we should require vendor-signed firmware for Dedicated fleets.
